title: 'Not great': October CPI inflation rises 0.4% as food and rent costs spike
summary:
Consumer Price Index data for October showed that inflation remains elevated, as costs rose across a wide range of essential goods and services, including food, rent, and medical care.
"Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, coming in ahead of the 0.2% economists were expecting to match September's level.
Owners' equivalent rent, which measures homeownership costs, rose 0.3%, while rents were up 0.2%.
Energy costs rose 0.7% last month, down from 5.2% in September.
Tuesday's inflation data is the Federal Reserve's final look at the CPI before it meets Dec. 8-9, although it will get another look at inflation data via its preferred measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index, later this month.

title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
summary:
Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly hightoggle caption i Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty ImagesInflation-scarred consumers are finding a bit of relief these days at an unlikely place: the gas pump.
Sponsor MessageWhy gas prices are fallingThe drop in gasoline prices in recent weeks is thanks to a combination of falling crude oil prices, refineries' switch to a cheaper blend of winter fuel, and the typical seasonal drop in demand for gas.
Diesel prices have also fallen, but more slowly than gas prices.
Heating oil prices are also highRising diesel prices are also driving up the cost of heating oil in the northeast, because heating oil is a close cousin of diesel.
Higher diesel prices also affect the cost of other goods that have to be moved by truck or train or cargo ship.

title: Consumer prices increased 0.4% in October, higher than expected
summary:
Consumer prices rose more than expected in October, according to a government report released on Tuesday.
The monthly increase in October matched the rise in August.
Prices for shelter increased 0.3% in October, accounting for more than 30% of the overall monthly rise in prices, the BLS said.
Prices increased 3.7% over the year ending in September, the most recent month for which annual inflation data is available.
The annual inflation rate currently stands more than a percentage point above the Federal Reserve's target rate of 2%.

title: US petrol prices are down, but elevated inflation continues
summary:
Inflation remained high, despite some easing in fuel prices caused by the US war on Iran.
Consumer prices in the United States increased in October more than expected, even as petrol prices fell to a four-month low after some easing of concerns about the long-term impact of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz on global markets.
But the average price, currently $3.98, is still significantly higher than the $3.07 mark it was at a year ago.
The average price of a gallon of petrol was $2.98 ($0.78 per litre) on February 28, when the US and Israel first struck Iran.

title: Jensen Huang Net Worth Drops, Out of Rich List Top 10 After Scandal
summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is no longer one of the world's 10 richest people.
Nvidia stock fell as much as 9% on Monday, before paring the loss to end 4.3% lower at $178.67 per share.
At the same time, Huang's net worth dropped $6.5 billion to $148 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
Huang was 10th when markets closed on Friday, and as recently as October, he was ranked 7th, with a net worth roughly $60 billion higher.
Huang's net worth is tied to Nvidia's stock, as he owns over 870 million shares, according to the company's latest annual report.

title: Economists Worry Fed Could Go Overboard With Rate Hikes After Hot CPI
summary:
October inflation data came in hot on Tuesday, with consumer prices rising 0.4% month over month.
The hot reading has prompted some senior Fed officials to strike a decidedly more hawkish tone this week.
Austan Goolsbee, the president of the Chicago Fed but not an FOMC voting member, called October's inflation print "borderline disturbing" in an interview with PBS Newshour on Tuesday.
